answers:
[goal] Reconcile June's 40 invoices against the bank statement and write the gaps to `./result.json`.

[action] Parsed every bank memo for a 4-digit invoice id in any format (`inv1007`, `INV-1015`, `invoice 1023`), grouped payments per invoice, then classified: no payment = unpaid; >1 payment = duplicated; exactly 1 payment with a differing amount = mismatched. Non-invoice lines ignored.

[result] Written to `./result.json`:
- unpaid: `INV-1008` (23,693.91), `INV-1030` (8,092.29), `INV-1033` (21,266.69)
- duplicated: `INV-1015` — paid twice, 2026-06-05 and 2026-06-17, 1,904.29 each
- mismatched: `INV-1021` invoiced 21,320.36 / paid 21,070.36 (short 250.00); `INV-1036` invoiced 8,619.16 / paid 7,757.24 (short 861.92)

[what I found and why it's right] All 40 invoice ids map to exactly one classification and every statement line is accounted for: 37 invoices paid at least once, 36 of those fully and exactly. The three ignored lines are `CDB INTEREST` (+1,204.33), `BANK SERVICE PACKAGE FEE` (-89.90) and `PIX received unidentified 1099` (1,500.00) — the README says to ignore fees, interest and PIX transfers without an identifiable invoice, and no INV-1099 exists. Assumptions: amounts compared to the cent (tolerance 0.005), "duplicated" means more than one payment regardless of amount, and categories are exclusive per the README — so INV-1015 is only duplicated even though both of its payments equal its invoice. Verified by re-reading the emitted JSON and printing the parsed object.

[next] None; hand `result.json` to Finance.
